title: Entanglement diagnostics of stochastic-resetting steady states: theory and measurement on superconducting qubits
authors: Jakob Murauer, Sabine Tornow, Manas Kulkarni, Eli Barkai, Satya N. Majumdar, Monalisa Singh Roy
abstract: Stochastic resetting drives quantum systems into nonequilibrium stationary states unreachable under uninterrupted unitary evolution, and their entanglement depends on whether the reset history is resolved or averaged over. We study this interplay in the transverse-field Ising chain, deriving closed-form results for two qubits and evaluating chains of up to 12 qubits exactly. In the two-qubit system, these closed-form results show that phase matching between energy eigenstates produces resonances, and their visibility in the stationary state is determined by the symmetry of the reset state. Measurements on an IBM superconducting processor show the entropies evaluated before and after the reset average closely following noiseless predictions with no fitted parameter, while concurrence lies below prediction across most of the hardware measurements. The two diagnostics respond differently because they read different components of the same reconstructed state, and a depolarizing model captures the concurrence suppression with one fitted parameter. The difference between the two entropies, i. e., the Jensen gap of entanglement entropy, equals the Holevo information that a subsystem retains about the time since the last reset. With a Bell-state reset, this information grows with chain length across a half-chain cut over the sizes studied, without visible saturation at the smaller reset probabilities. Since reset times are sampled and recorded classically, the trajectory-averaged entropy, and with it the Jensen gap, is obtained without postselection, in contrast to monitored circuits, where trajectory-resolved entanglement requires sampling exponentially rare measurement records.
summary: This work analyzes entanglement in quantum systems driven into non-equilibrium steady states via stochastic resetting. By comparing theoretical predictions for the transverse-field Ising chain with superconducting qubit measurements, the authors show that different entanglement diagnostics (like entropy vs. concurrence) respond differently to the reset process. The key finding establishes a direct physical interpretation for the difference between averaged and trajectory-averaged entanglement measures.
main_problem: The paper investigates how entanglement diagnostics behave in non-equilibrium steady states generated by stochastic resetting protocols.
main_result: The Jensen gap of entanglement entropy equals the Holevo information quantifying subsystem memory of the reset time, and this information grows with chain length for a Bell-state reset.
method: The authors derive closed-form theoretical results for the transverse-field Ising chain and validate them by performing measurements on an IBM superconducting quantum processor.
model_or_system: The system is the transverse-field Ising chain, subjected to a discrete-time stochastic resetting protocol. The dynamics are governed by a mixture of unitary evolution and resetting to a fixed state.
key_observables: Averaged-state entropy, trajectory-averaged entropy, Wootters concurrence, and the Jensen gap of entanglement entropy.
important_parameters: Reset probability ($p$), coupling ratio ($\alpha$), and chain length ($N$, up to 12).
main_assumptions: The trajectory-averaged entropy is obtained without postselection, unlike monitored circuits which require sampling rare measurement records.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the quantum circuit implementing the discrete-time reset protocol and the associated geometric distribution of the system's 'age' (time since last reset).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework for stochastic resetting, deriving exact results for small systems. It then compares these theory results against hardware measurements on superconducting qubits, focusing on the differential behavior of entropy diagnostics versus concurrence.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, measurable link between non-equilibrium statistical mechanics (stochastic resetting) and quantum information measures (entanglement), using superconducting qubits as a testbed.
